about: Part of the reference catalogue: the case studies, designs and worked examples of the 11 chapters of Goos and Jones,
Optimal Design of Experiments: A Case Study Approach (2011), for testing that software reproduces them. source: the
citation, with what was read and when. experiments: the extraction experiment of chapter 2, the same experiment
augmented with eight runs in chapter 3, the peel strength experiment of chapter 4, the yield of a reaction over a
square and over a constrained region in chapter 5, the rolling mill of chapter 6, a mixture with process variables,
the experiments in blocks of chapters 7 and 8, the pastry dough and the stability of riboflavin, the polypropylene
experiment with covariates of chapter 9, the wind tunnel split-plot experiment of chapter 10 and the battery cell
two-way split-plot experiment of chapter 11, each with its
factors, responses and runs as printed, where it is printed, and expected: every number the book prints for it, as
printed text, with where it is printed (a page and a quotation) and check: how to recompute it, or manual, the reason
it is not recomputed. A check with a disagreement records a number known not to reproduce and why. The book fits
every model in coded units, except chapter 4's prediction equations and chapter 6's mixture models, which are in
pseudocomponents, and its VIF is n times a coefficient's variance in units of sigma squared (Equation 2.13): the
library's coefficient variance from evaluate_design's information_matrix, times the run count. Random block effects
and whole plots, and a two-way split-plot design's crossed rows and columns, are fitted by REML with JMP's
Kenward-Roger standard errors and degrees of freedom from the observed
information (split_plot), and a VIF or efficiency factor due to blocking is a coefficient's variance with the blocks
as fixed effects over its variance without them (relative_to). A split-plot design is evaluated through the
generalized least squares information X'V^-1 X, V = I + eta ZZ' (evaluate_design's random_effects, with the runs'
column of whole plots in groups), and a run order's robustness to a time trend by Equation 9.19 (trend_robustness). An
alias matrix printed in thirds is compared entry by entry as arithmetic (expression). Table 3.1's AICc is the model
summary's aicc, and Table 3.2's recommended settings the corner of the six factors where each model predicts the most
yield (best_corner). designs: the splits of chapter 1's runs between two machines or two treatments (allocate_runs),
Table 2.4's bias calculation (product_column), the four-run design of Table 2.8, the D-optimal design of Table
2.11, the designs of the coordinate-exchange example, each compared on |X'X|, chapter 4's D-optimal and I-optimal
designs, compared on their relative variances, their average prediction variance, their FDS plots and each other
(relative_efficiency), chapter 6's half fraction of the 2^5 factorial, the blocked designs of chapters 7 and 8, the
samples and the second design of chapter 9 and its trend-robust run orders, the split-plot designs of chapter 10, and
the two-way split-plot designs of chapter 11, evaluated with the rows and the columns as random effects.
not_captured: what in these pages is not an experiment with data. Read with
process_improve.experiments.reference_catalogue.reference_experiments; tests/test_reference_catalogue.py recomputes
every number that has a check.

design.type: 12-run two-level orthogonal design, one that can be derived from a Plackett-Burman design
design.details: made by a computer algorithm for a D-optimal design for the main-effects model; six factors, 12 runs, no replicates and no centre runs

runs.notes: Table 2.3 in its printed order; its settings are those of Table 2.2, and Table 2.1 prints the same runs coded −1 and +1 (a solvent absent and present, pH and time at their low and high levels)

experiments.notes: The book fits every model in coded units, x = (setting − centre)/(half the range), the factors x1 to x6 in the order of the columns. GeneBe's current process, methanol at neutral pH for 2 hours, yields about 25 mg; management wants more than 45 mg; at most 15 runs could be afforded, of which 12 are run and three kept for a confirmatory experiment. Dr. Zheng's model (Equation 2.1) keeps the main effects significant at the 5% level in the main-effects model, and the design being orthogonal, their coefficients are the same as in that model. The book's VIF is n times a coefficient's relative variance, its variance in units of σ² (Equation 2.13), checked as the library's coefficient variance times the run count.

experiments.title: The extraction experiment augmented with eight D-optimal runs, to tell nine competing models apart

factors.name: methanol
factors.description: methanol in the solvent system: absent (0) or present (10 ml), x1

factors.name: ethanol
factors.description: ethanol in the solvent system: absent (0) or present (10 ml), x2

factors.name: propanol
factors.description: propanol in the solvent system: absent (0) or present (10 ml), x3

factors.name: butanol
factors.description: butanol in the solvent system: absent (0) or present (10 ml), x4

factors.name: pH
factors.description: pH of the culture during the extraction, x5

factors.name: block
factors.description: x7, the experiment a run belongs to: 1 the original screening runs, coded +1, and 2 the follow-up runs, coded -1

responses.name: yield
responses.description: yield of the lipopeptide extracted from 100 ml of culture, measured by HPLC

design.type: a 12-run orthogonal design augmented with 8 runs chosen for a D-optimal design, in two blocks
design.details: the 12 runs of Table 2.3 and 8 follow-up runs chosen to maximise |X'X| for the main effects, six two-factor interactions and a block effect (Equation 3.5)

runs.notes: Table 3.5 in its printed order: runs 1 to 12 are the original experiment (Table 2.3), and runs 13 to 20 the follow-up; Table 3.3 prints the same runs before the follow-up's yields were measured

experiments.notes: The book codes every factor -1 and +1, and the block +1 for the original runs and -1 for the follow-up (x7). Tables 3.1, 3.2 and 3.6 are fitted to the 12 original runs, the rest to all 20. Models 1, 7 and 8 of Table 3.1 hold the ethanol-by-propanol interaction without propanol's main effect: weak heredity. Table 3.6's caption names the interaction 'ethanol and butanol'; its row is ethanol by propanol, as Table 2.6's. Table 3.4's power is that of the t-test at the 5% level of a coefficient as large as the error's standard deviation, on the 6 degrees of freedom the 20 runs leave the 14-term model. The VIF is the book's, n times a relative variance.

experiments.title: Stability of riboflavin in light: a 32-run D-optimal screening design in eight blocks (days) of four for six two-level factors

factors.name: boundedness
factors.description: riboflavin free or bounded in a complex with gamma-cyclodextrin, x1

factors.name: oil_red_o
factors.description: Oil Red O, a light-absorbing fatty molecule, out or in, x2

factors.name: beta_carotene
factors.description: beta carotene, out or in, x4

factors.name: block
factors.description: the day, on which the measuring apparatus is calibrated

responses.name: stability_ratio
responses.description: stability ratio of the riboflavin; 200 and more is desirable

design.type: D-optimal design in blocks
design.details: 32 runs for six main effects and 15 two-factor interactions, in eight blocks (days) of four

runs.notes: Table 8.9 in its printed order: the runs of Table 8.4, x1 to x6 the six factors in this order, Complex and In coded +1

experiments.notes: Each factor is coded -1 and +1, Free or Out at -1, as JMP codes a two-level categorical factor, so Boundedness[Complex] is half the effect. The fixed block effects analysis (Table 8.10) is least squares with the blocks coded to sum to zero; the random block effects analysis (Table 8.11) is REML with JMP's Kenward-Roger standard errors and degrees of freedom, computed from the observed information. The text says the sixth factor is whether the vitamin was free or complexed; it is the first column of Table 8.9.

experiments.name: goos-jones-wind-tunnel
experiments.title: Drag, lift and efficiency of a race car in a wind tunnel: a 50-run I-optimal split-plot design in ten whole plots, two hard-to-change factors

factors.name: frh
factors.description: front ride height, hard to change (x1)

factors.name: rrh
factors.description: rear ride height, hard to change (x2)

factors.name: grille
factors.description: grille tape coverage of the lower cooling inlet, easy to change (x4)

responses.name: lift_front
responses.description: coefficient of lift over the front axle, CLF

responses.name: lift_rear
responses.description: coefficient of lift over the rear axle, CLR

design.type: I-optimal split-plot design
design.details: ten settings of the two ride heights (the 3^2 factorial and its centre once more), five runs of yaw angle and grille tape coverage in each, I-optimal for the full quadratic model with the whole-plot and run variances equal

runs.notes: Table 10.4 in its printed order: setting is the whole plot, the hard-to-change factor setting of Table 10.2, which prints the same runs coded

experiments.notes: The book fits every model in coded units. The ordinary least squares fits (Tables 10.5 and 10.7) ignore the whole plots; the generalized least squares fits (Tables 10.6 to 10.8) are REML with the settings as random whole plots, with JMP's Kenward-Roger standard errors and degrees of freedom from the observed information. The total lift of Table 10.8 is the front lift plus the rear lift, run by run. Table 10.3's variances are those of the generalized least squares information X'V^-1 X with V = I + ZZ', the whole-plot and run variances both one.
